[h1][i]«На хитрого минёра, сапёров не напасёшься.»[/i][/h1]

Эй, народ! Давайте я вам расскажу про свою жизнь в игре "Сапер". Да-да, именно в той, где вам нужно шагать по минным полям, воробьи восторженно щебечут, а ты, как будто стал майором спецназа, пытаешься разобраться, где тут прячутся эти коварные мины! Зачем мне, спросите вы, это вообще нужно? Хм, просто потому, что я упрямый, и кто-то же должен разбираться в этих подземных ловушках, а так как у меня нет диплома сапера, то я просто взял на себя эту роль!

Первое, что я заметил, когда зашел в эту игру — это графика. Я понимаю, что игра старенькая, но эй, давайте будем честными, нам это не мешало на уроках информатики в школе, не так ли? Пиксели были в моде! И вот я вижу, как меня окружает игровое поле, покрытое загадочными цифрами и запутанными клетками. Каждая они выглядит так, будто кусочки головоломки осталось недосказать. Зная, что в каждой клеточке прячется невидимая угроза, я словно начинаю игру в "Тайны нации". Я такой: «О, что мы тут имеем?» Цифры и все такое… Это что, календара? Нет, это просто мои шансы на выживание!

И вот начинается веселье: я должен втыкать в эти клетки, как будто решаю задачу на экзамене по математике, и... БУМ! Мина! Чёрт! Как же так?! В момент, когда я нажимаю на клетку, где явно не ожидал взрыва, я понимаю, что "Сапер" — это не только игра, а настоящая проверка на терпение и жизненные навыки! Я должен разгадывать, как где-то под этими клетками витают бомбы, как будто в моем доме с подружкой, когда она решила оставить свои вещи на полу!

Но знаете, в этом есть что-то интересное: читать эти цифры и вычислять, где же спрятаны мины — это как играть в шпионские игры! Какой-то миссионер запутанных маршрутов! Златая охота на сокровища с этим чудесным детским азартом. Я прокладываю путь к победе, как будто собираю артефакты в шутере! Если ты хоть раз видишь цифру «1» рядом, это настолько же захватывающе, как если бы ты открыл страницу крутого комикса с супергероями!

В общем, если хочешь проверить свою интуицию, стратегическое мышление, и в то же время повеселиться, "Сапер" — это то, что надо! Не забывайте, что одно неверное движение — и вы расстаетесь с жизнью! И кто знал, что мины могут быть такими игривыми? Так что одевайте свои шпионские шляпы и готовьтесь к борьбе с минными полями. Помните, друзья, жизнь — это не всегда путь вокруг мин, иногда стоит просто рискнуть и пойти на них!

While the premise of the game is a new age version of Minesweeper, I just didn't find it challenging enough to really recommend.

In this iteration of the game, you have to find bombs by tagging areas that you believe are bombs and chipping away at the areas that are not bombs.  Numbers will show up to let you know how many bombs surround the square that you've uncovered.  Simple, basic concept of the well known game that this is made to be.

Additional things have been added to the game such as lives.  You can even collect different bonuses to either recover your life entirely or add lives to your hit point counter so you can click on bombs and not die, but live to try another square.  While this may add a quality of life it does not change anything else, hence makes the game even less of a challenge than the original game.

You can either play the main game or a custom game, the main game gets increasingly more difficult, while the custom game allows you to play one game and be out.  Though overall, the custom games allow you to create impossible games that aren't even fun at all.  For example, 36 squares with 34 bombs leaving you with 2 squares to click on.  The first click is always clear of any bombs, so good luck finding the next square to click on out of the potentially 35 remaining squares.  The game should have created a better ratio or a better ability to create custom games.  Even the original Minesweeper did this better than this version of it.

As a whole there are much better games of this type out there that you can purchase such as Globesweeper.  If you're into casual puzzle games, then go for it, if you are looking for a challenge, then look elsewhere.

FineSweeper ist ein Rätsel-Spiel und im Prinzip eine weiter entwickelte Variante von Minesweeper, was alte Hasen noch kennen dürften. Junge Hasen können sicher auch Spaß an dem Spiel haben. Die Zahlen deuten an, wie viele Minen im Umfeld dieser Zahl sind, das heißt mit anderen Worten, wenn eine 1 zu sehen ist, dann ist eine Mine in den 8 Feldern um der Eins. Mit logischen Rückschlüssen kann man dann mehr und mehr vom Spielfeld aufdecken.

Grafisch ist das Spiel sehr rudimentär gehalten, wie Minesweeper damals eben auch. Mehr braucht es auch nicht. Dabei ist es aber optisch weitaus ansprechender als die alte Vorlage. Die Bomben sehen besser aus und die Explosionen auch. Auch soundtechnisch klingen die Explosionen besser, weil sie überhaupt klingen und im Hintergrund läuft eine Musik, die mit der Zeit ggf. nervig werden könnte.

Durch die Leben, die man bekommen kann, ist das Spiel nicht so unfair wie die ehemalige Variante. Manchmal kann man auch logischen Schlüssen nicht herausfinden, wo genau eine Bombe liegt. Dann muss man raten. Wenn man daneben liegt, werden die Zahlen angepasst, weil nun eine Bombe weniger auf dem Feld ist. Das finde ich sehr praktisch. Wer also den Klassiker damals sehr gut fand, der kann hier gerne zuschlagen. Es ist halt Minesweeper in guter Optik. Das möchte das Spiel sein und das ist das Spiel.

Back in the 90s, Minesweeper was the ultimate test of intelligence, patience, and whether you could left-click faster than your mistakes. It came pre-installed on every Windows machine, lurking quietly next to Solitaire, ready to ruin your day with a single misstep. And now… it’s back. But fancier.

Fine Sweeper is like someone took that dusty old relic of a game, gave it a monocle, a top hat, and taught it how to strut.

🎮 Same addicting gameplay – The core is pure Minesweeper. Numbers, bombs, logic, panic.
🧠 Now with upgrades – RPG-style progression, unlockable perks, and tools that actually help (take that, 50/50 guesses!).
🧥 Pixel-perfect presentation – Retro-style graphics with slick animations and just the right amount of nostalgia.
📀 Soundtrack goes hard – Far better than the "you exploded, silence now" treatment of the original.

There's even a story mode. A story mode, in Minesweeper. I didn’t know I needed this until I played it.

It’s like returning to your childhood home and finding out someone added central heating, a coffee bar, and a loot system.

Pros:
✅ Finally a Minesweeper that rewards you for being good at it
✅ Smart modern touches without ruining the classic feel
✅ Secretly makes you feel like a bomb defusal expert
✅ Nostalgia, but with perks!

Cons:
❌ Still can’t escape the occasional 50/50 guess
❌ No office job to pretend I’m working at while playing

If you ever lost hours to the original Minesweeper and wished it had more depth, personality, or explosions with context, Fine Sweeper delivers in spades.

💣💥 10/10 – The 90s called. They said this is way better.

Minesweeper + Quality of Life Improvements = Fine Sweeper
---

If it wasn't obvious enough from the store page, Fine Sweeper could easily be called a clone of Minesweeper. But it's not quite a clone, it's a much improved variant that offers a greater sense of progression, less random failures (that aren't your fault) and numerous other (minor) improvements that total up to a much better game than the one it's cloned from.

If you already know what Minesweeper is and want a better version of it, this is a no brainer. It's a cheap and pleasant way to kill some time and play with brain teasing puzzles.

If you aren't familiar with Minesweeper, it's a classic game that used to be included with early versions of Windows operating systems to give people a fun way to practice their mouse clicking skills (yes, prior to a mouse being a ubiquitous and common tool, people honestly didn't know how to use the thing well). These days (for whatever reason) it's no longer included by default with Windows 10, but can be found for free through various sources.

Sometimes you just want a simple relaxing series of puzzles to chip away the hours.

Did you enjoy minesweeper?  This game is a minesweeper variant with extra features. You get lives, there’s score keeping and of course Achievements. As a fan of minesweeper I really enjoyed the game. 

Gameplay -  9

This is a pretty niche type of game. If you don’t like minesweeper you probably won’t care for this game. If you have never played the game the basic idea is that you are sweeping for mines.  You pick a square and if it’s not a mine. Good job. If it is you blow up. Now if it’s not a bomb it will either be a blank space or a space with a number in it.  If it’s blank. Move on to another space. The number tells you how many mines are in the 8 squares around that 1 square.  From there it’s just using logic to figure out where the mines are located. 

Story -  N/A



Graphics -  8

Pretty decent, easy to read and there is no confusion.  Not much else to say. 


Controls - MouseKeyboard -10

You left click to uncover a single square, right click to mark mines. Left and right click on a number, that already has associated mines marked,  and it’ll clear out all the area it can around. 
That’s pretty much it, you can also mark ?’s but I take off that feature in options. 

Repeatability - 8

It’s mine sweeper, you’re going to be playing the levels over and over.  There’s an achievement to get to level 7 in less than 1 minute. Not impossible, but difficult enough that you’ll be playing the first 6 levels over and over a few times. 



Music - ???

It’s there? Usually while gaming I listen to my own music, unless it’s a sound based game. 

Multiplayer - N/A 

Pretty sure there is not multiplayer, but there are online leaderboards.


Initial Thoughts:

Soma Says: 

Normally I like to put in a good 10 or so hours into a game before reviewing it.  However, this game is an easy exception. I’ve put 100’s if not 1000’s into the original minesweeper.  I live an exciting life as you can tell. 

The addition of extra lives is a good one, it’s frustrating to hit a mine because you made a stupid mistake and have to start all over. This is just a more forgiving version of minesweeper.

Fine Sweeper è un gioco gustoso che regala molte emozioni ed è utile a chi deve affrontare l'esame di Analisi 2 in Ingegneria. Per pochi euro potrete raggiungere, con solo due ore giornaliere di allenamento su questo gioco, lo stesso QI di Stiven Okking che dall'alto del cielo vi proteggerà e vi regalerà sane emozioni al gusto di fragola.

Il gioco fila liscio il frame rate stabile sui 60 fps (ricordiamo che l'occhio umano non vede oltre) ci regala la fluidità nelle animazioni fatte da 2 frame che andranno smooth anche sui calcolatori più deboli grazie al grande lavoro di ottimizzazione fatto dagli sviluppatori.

Questo T I T O L O è di una vastità e profondità di gameplay talmente alta e deep che le menti più geniali troveranno comunque divertimento nell'affrontare la sfida principale del gioco. Peccato l'assenza di modalità aggiuntive e di una modalità multi player.

In sintesi, tornando a noi, vi sconsiglio di comprarlo perché si potrebbe rivelare più pericoloso del crocodile.

Game is fun for a while, but on reflection it's not that much different from playing Windows Minesweeper. Has cards and achievements, and is a little more lenient because you have lives, I suppose.

Personally I found the soundtrack really annoying, so I turned it off. Dev was kind enough to show me how to hide/turn off the timer, which was nice.

My reccomendation is still a no though. What I disliked about the game most was still the feeling of time pressure. As someone with anxiety, it's just not for me. If you like that kind of thing in your games though, then by all means go for it.

It's minesweeper but with the ability to make mistakes and keep going thanks to its life system. This addition has two benefits: first, it helps you overcome the frustration the classic windows time waster could  bring when you had a promising run stopped abrubtly by an impossible-to-guess mine. Second, it adds a new level of strategy missing from the original game since you can use your lives as a resource to maximize the information you get from an explosion. Overall, this version keeps the core addictive gameplay of the original while adding much needed improvements.
